title: From the ARP Odyssey to the ODYSSEY
intro: The ARP Odyssey was ARP Instruments’ answer to the Minimoog: a portable, duophonic synth whose modules are wired inside and set by sliders and switches, the 2600’s ideas without the patch cords. It went through three revisions, each with a different filter. Behringer’s ODYSSEY copies the last of them and puts all three filters on one switch, adding a sequencer, an arpeggiator and Klark Teknik effects.

timeline.name: ARP 2600
timeline.text: ARP’s semi-modular: three VCOs, a filter, two envelopes, sample and hold and a ring modulator, pre-wired and set by sliders. The Odyssey takes its voice and fixes the routing behind switches.

timeline.name: ARP Odyssey Mk I
timeline.text: Two VCOs, duophonic, a sample and hold, a ring modulator, a high-pass after the low-pass, and an ADSR and an AR, in a white-faced case. Its low-pass is the 2-pole 4023.

timeline.name: ARP Odyssey Mk II
timeline.text: A black-and-gold panel and a 4-pole filter, the 4035, a ladder design. ARP replaced it with its own 4075 after Moog objected that it copied the patented ladder.

timeline.name: ARP Odyssey Mk III
timeline.text: The black-and-orange panel the ODYSSEY copies, the 4075 filter, and the PROPORTIONAL PITCH CONTROL pads in place of a bend knob. ARP closed in 1981.

timeline.name: Korg ARP Odyssey
timeline.text: A reissue made with ARP’s co-founder David Friend, on a smaller keyboard, with the three revisions’ filters on one switch.

timeline.name: Behringer ODYSSEY
timeline.text: The Mk III panel on 37 full-size keys, the three filters on one switch, drive, a 32-step sequencer with 64 patterns, an eight-mode arpeggiator, and 32 Klark Teknik effects.

relatives.name: Behringer 2600
relatives.text: Behringer’s copy of the ARP 2600, the Odyssey’s parent: the same kind of voice with every connection breakable by a patch cord. This app plays it too.

relatives.name: ARP Axxe
relatives.text: ARP’s smaller sibling: one VCO, the same slider-and-switch layout, and a sample and hold.

relatives.name: Minimoog Model D
relatives.text: The portable monosynth the Odyssey was built to compete with. This app plays the Model D.
